title: Lane-specific Hosted Endpoint SLA and Minimal Acceptance Kit
creator: Aisha Kaur
overview: This ticket captures a compact Product Requirements Document and a minimal go-live acceptance kit for lane-specific hosted endpoints (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank). The goal is to define per-lane behavioral contracts, SLOs, test artifacts, and an actionable launch checklist that enables shipping with guardrails and rapid rollback paths. This does not cover Dedicated or Private deployment variants other than where explicitly noted.
goals: Define SLA lanes (gold/silver/beta) for hosted inference endpoints with measurable SLOs and clear degradation behavior
Provide a minimal set of automated and manual acceptance checks (the Acceptance Kit) that engineering and SRE can run pre- and post- rollout
Ensure API surface compatibility for current integrations and add guidance for soft-breaking changes with migration paths
Ship a go-live runbook that coordinates console, docs, billing, and monitoring ownership
out_of_scope: Dedicated capacity contract negotiations and quota plumbing
Model architecture changes or large-scale quantization initiatives (these are handled by runtime/model onboarding teams)
functional_requirements: Endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank must expose consistent auth, billing metadata, and request/response shapes per API contract
Backwards compatibility: existing client SDK calls must succeed for the current public parameter set unless marked deprecated and gated by feature flags
Graceful fallback: when a lane cannot meet latency/capacity SLO, requests must be automatically routed to the next compatible lane or return a deterministic 503 with structured retry headers
Streaming: chat streaming must preserve token ordering and offer both chunked newline-delimited and event-stream styles for SDKs
Rerank: /v1/rerank must accept batched candidate lists and return stable score ordering; documentation must include complexity and cost guidance
nonfunctional_requirements: SLOs by lane (see SLA_LANES field): targets must be measured and reported in Console dashboards
Per-tenant throttling and quota enforcement must be in place with transparent error codes and retry headers
Audit logging: request-level metadata (tenant-id, model-id, lane, latency_ms) stored for 90 days for debugging
Privacy/compliance: PII-free telemetry by default; customer PII only captured when explicitly enabled by customers and encrypted-at-rest
Latency budgets should be adjustable per-lane and exposed via an API for operator automation
sla_lanes: gold: targeted at mission-critical customers; throughput-backed reservations in Dedicated-like pools when requested; SLOs: p50 token latency < 60ms, p95 < 250ms, availability 99.95%
silver: general hosted usage; SLOs: p50 token latency < 120ms, p95 < 500ms, availability 99.9%
beta: experimental/new-model lanes; best-effort latency and 99.5% availability with explicit communicated degradations
acceptance_kit: Contract tests: automated suites that validate request/response shapes, error codes, and header invariants for each endpoint
Performance smoke: synthetic workload that exercises realistic token distributions for short, medium, long sequences; verifies lane SLOs over a 30-minute window
Stability run: 6-hour soak test at 2x expected peak traffic for the initial cohort; must produce no P0 incidents and <1% error rate
Fallback verification: induce a simulated capacity loss and verify deterministic routing to fallback lane or 503 behavior
Security sanity: run automated SAST on endpoint code and validate IAM/KMS integration for tenant-scoped keys
Docs & SDK: public API docs drafted, SDKs (python/js) updated with compatibility tests and release notes ready
api_surface_expectations: Unified auth header (Authorization: Bearer) and explicit Tenant-ID header for multi-tenant routing
Consistent usage metadata in responses (X-Model-ID, X-Lane, X-Request-Cost) to support billing and observability
Structured error model: machine-readable error codes, retry-after, and human-friendly messages
Feature flags to gate new fields (e.g., structured output, function-calling) per-tenant during rollout
acceptance_criteria: All contract tests pass in staging for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank and are green in CI for two consecutive runs
Performance smoke shows lane SLO attainment within 10% margin for the intended initial customer cohort
Observability: dashboards for per-lane latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token-per-request distributions, and cost-per-token are created and shared
Runbook & rollback: a tested rollback path exists that can flip traffic by model or lane within 5 minutes via a single operator action
Documentation: public API docs, migration notes, and an SDK compatibility table published prior to soft-launch
Billing: cost-metering validated against synthetic workloads and billing hooks confirmable in sandbox accounts
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood — 1 week with platform teams and top internal integrations to flush runtime issues
Phase 1: Beta customers (invite-only) at 5% of ingress traffic for 72 hours, monitor SLOs and error modes
Phase 2: Gradual increase to 25% over 48 hours if no critical regressions; open opt-in to selected customers
Phase 3: Regional ramp + feature flag unlocks for structured output and function-calling per lane
Phase 4: Full public availability after 14 days of stable metrics and post-launch retrospective
launch_checklist: API docs published and linked in Console onboarding flow
SDK releases (python/js) with clear changelog and deprecation notices ready
Console: per-lane toggles in the control plane to pin lanes, set local quotas, and toggle fallbacks
Billing: pricing table entries for each lane and telemetry validated in billing pipelines
Monitoring: dashboards and alerting configured (severity mapping to on-call teams)
Runbook: step-by-step runbook published in Confluence with links to emergency rollback playbooks and paging lists
Legal & Compliance: privacy checklist signed off for hosted telemetry and retention policies
Customer communications: beta invites, changelog, and migration guidance drafted and scheduled
Launch window: coordinated with infra (maintenance windows avoided) and support teams staffed for 72 hours post-launch
monitoring_and_alerts: Per-lane SLOs with burn-rate alerts: trigger paging at 3x burn for p95 latency or sustained error rate >1%
Anomaly detection on model-level token costs and sudden increases in average tokens per request
Synthetic canary jobs per region and lane running every 2 minutes with end-to-end validation
Audit log integrity monitor to detect missing request-level metadata ingestion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unanticipated tail latency under realistic conversational workloads. Mitigation: conservative initial lane caps and aggressive KV cache tuning during beta
Risk: Customer confusion over lane guarantees. Mitigation: concise lane-level docs and in-console explanations plus default lane recommendations for new accounts
Risk: Billing mismatch due to mis-attributed tokens. Mitigation: shadow-meter production traffic in billing sandbox and reconcile prior to GA
Risk: New API fields breaking clients. Mitigation: default-to-backwards-compatible behavior and opt-in feature flags with clear SDK release notes
dependencies: ENG-81902: per-tenant quota enforcement and throttle headers
PM-991200: pricing model finalization for lane-based billing
